name: Finite Auxiliary Bounds at a Prescribed Parent Rank
statement: Let $\varnothing\ne C\subsetneq\{0,1\}^X$ and fix $r\ge0$. If a minimally missing pattern has support larger than $r+1$, no rank-$r$ maximum parent exists. Otherwise put $B_r(C)=\sum_{p\in\mathcal M(C)}(r+1-|\operatorname{supp}p|)$ and $D_r(C)=(r+1)|\{0,1\}^X\setminus C|-e_\partial(C)$. If a rank-$r$ parent exists then $D_r(C)\ge0$, and some rank-$r$ parent with the same visible labels and section uses at most $\min(B_r(C),D_r(C))$ auxiliaries. Consequently existence at any specified rank is decidable by finite enumeration.
proof: Every minimal missing visible pattern extends, together with part of the auxiliary mark, to the unique missing pattern on an $(r+1)$-support of the maximum parent. Retaining the union of these auxiliary supports preserves every forbidden visible word and hence the exact section, giving $B_r$. Alternatively choose one parent witness per absent full word. Every boundary coordinate toward $C$ must occur visibly in that witness, leaving at most $r+1-d_C(x)$ auxiliary entries; summing gives $D_r$. These finite bounds reduce rank-$r$ existence to enumerating finitely many marked maximum classes.
